edges.description: Systemic PQBP1 dysfunction impairs somatic growth, resulting in short stature.
Developmental gene dysregulation caused by PQBP1 deficiency leads to characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism.
PQBP1 deficiency affects male gonadal development, resulting in small testes.
Perturbed organogenesis from PQBP1 deficiency can manifest with ocular developmental anomalies including microphthalmia.
Perturbed cardiac morphogenesis from PQBP1 deficiency can lead to congenital heart defects such as atrial septal defect.
Developmental dysregulation caused by pathogenic PQBP1 variants rarely includes anorectal malformation.
Gain-of-function preservation of proliferative alternative polyadenylation profiles impedes the transition from apical to basal neural progenitors.

evidence.snippet: Renpenning syndrome (OMIM: 309500) is a rare X-linked intellectual disability caused by variations in the polyglutamine-binding protein 1 (PQBP1) gene, characterized by moderate to severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, short stature, lean body, small testes, and abnormal facial features.

nodes.description: In addition to partial loss-of-function from protein misfolding, the pathogenic PQBP1 p.Tyr65Cys (Y65C) missense variant exerts a gain-of-function effect by enhancing interactions with core components of the mRNA 3'-end processing machinery, preserving proliferative alternative polyadenylation (APA) profiles and impeding apical-to-basal neural progenitor transition; the net directional effect on mRNA binding across PQBP1 alleles is marked abnormal rather than strictly increased or decreased.
